evidence.quote: Running two systems at one desk for a few weeks is a known, contained pain with a named owner. Two cutovers landing in the same week is an unbounded one, and we've got nobody to hand it to.

observations.why: Tanya frames the decision around risk containment, predictability, and stability over unbounded operational risk.

evidence.quote: My argument is that a four-minute-stale number is fine and an outage is not.

observations.why: Xavier explicitly values system stability and outage prevention over fresh data.

evidence.quote: Keeping one source of truth through the whole programme is worth more than getting ownership early.

observations.why: Xavier explicitly prioritizes data consistency and single-source stability over early autonomy or ownership.

mints.name: ContainmentOverSpeed
mints.title: contained risk prioritized over speed or early ownership
mints.frame: Does this expression explicitly justify a tradeoff by elevating operational stability and blast-radius containment above velocity or control?
